direct_comparison.1.32.15a: yātáḥ, present active genitive singular, in contrast with avasitasya in the same pāda.
direct_comparison.1.141.8a: The same accent-bearing word-form label yātáḥ is a ta-participle, masculine nominative singular, beside rathaḥ in its clause.
direct_comparison.10.85.12a: yātyā́ḥ is expressly feminine genitive singular in the wedding chariot verse. It selects the branch without the optional n.
direct_comparison.1.117.12a: yā́ntā is a masculine nominative dual beside kuha. Against the ordinary yāntau there is a Vedic -ā ending; compare 7.1.39.
